messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I’m seeing a perf regression in the AWQ int8 weight-only path on the short-seq chat benchmark. ~10% tail latency bump compared to last week. Not constant, spikes on cold KV-cache hits.
aj: Can you paste the bench numbers and config? sequence length, batch, group_size, pack mode?
maria: Sure. Baseline (last-good): group_size=64, prepack=true, pack-on-load. New run: group_size=128, prepack=false (we were testing memory). Short-seq (seq=32), batch=8. Median latency: baseline 48ms -> new 52ms. P95: 120ms -> 132ms. Throughput roughly same.
ryan: Interesting — did kernel selection change? Sometimes the selector prefers a simpler kernel that avoids prepacked weight path, which increases per-request pack overhead.
sophia: Do you have a profiler trace? even small pack_time_us add up for chat workloads.
maria: Yep, pasted below (trimmed):
```
Profile sample (seq=32,batch=8,group=128):
- weight_pack_time_us: 118.4
- kernel_exec_us (int8_packed_v2): 42.1
- kernel_exec_us (int8_unpacked_fallback): 48.7
- total_per_token_us: 0.86
Note: pack called on first token for each allocation - KV-cache miss path.
```
aj: pack_time 118us is huge relative to kernel_exec. For short outputs that's dominating tail. If prepack=true the pack_time becomes near zero at inference time.
ryan: Another datapoint: When group_size increases to 128, packing is more expensive (more blocks), and our current pack routine is O(groupsize) rather than optimized loops for big groups. That explains increased pack_time. Also AWQ's layout for group=128 triggers a slower memcpy pattern in our packer.
sophia: Two paths to try: (1) prefer prepack during kernel selection when expected token count per request < threshold, (2) add a micro-batching penalty to kernel score for pack-on-demand so selector favors prepacked kernels for chat workloads.
maria: I tried quick ablation: set group_size=64 but keep prepack=false. Latency improved ~6% from the regression point (not fully back to baseline because pack still happens but fewer groups).
aj: We should also check GPTQ artifact — GPTQ weight layout is slightly different so our packer chooses a different codepath. Did you test AWQ vs GPTQ?
maria: Yes. GPTQ (group=128) had smaller pack_time (~70us) but slightly worse kernel_exec (50us). Net effect similar but distribution different. AWQ pack path is the culprit.
ryan: Proposed fixes:
- Short term: change kernel selector to prefer prepacked kernels when estimated tokens_per_req < 64 or when expected KV-cache miss probability > 0.2.
- Medium: micro-optimizations in packer for AWQ group multiples (vectorize memcpy, reduce allocations).
- Long: add a prepack-on-load flag in runtime that precomputes packed weights for models uploaded with AWQ/GPTQ variants.
sophia: Also tweak batching heuristic: for chat workloads we currently batch aggressively up to batch=16. But if pack_time is non-trivial, grouping small concurrent requests into one pack call could help — e.g., batch pack calls for requests arriving within 5ms window. Might need small concurrency semaphore.
maria: Repro command I used: `./perf_driver --model redwood-awq-7b --quant awq --group_size 128 --prepack false --seq 32 --batch 8 --profile out.json`
ryan: Good. Can we run two A/B runs: (A) enable prepack=true, group=128; (B) keep prepack=false but set selector threshold tokens_per_req<64 -> prefer prepacked kernel. Compare p95/p99 and cost per token.
aj: I can schedule runs on prod-like infra. deploy-bot: Scheduling perf jobs: tag=awq-latency-calib-177888, jobs=4, target=prod-like-gpu-pool, eta=30m.
deploy-bot: Job started: 177888-1 (A: prepack=true), 177888-2 (B: selector-rule).
maria: After 2 runs: A (prepack=true) median 47ms, p95 118ms. B (selector-rule) median 49ms, p95 125ms. So prepack still best but selector rule recovers most of the win without memory change.
sophia: That suggests runtime selector change is lowest friction. We should add a small feature flag and rollout to canary. Also track memory delta for prepack.
ryan: I'll open a PR to the kernel-selector: add `pack_penalty_us` estimation in scoring, incorporate expected packs_per_req = 1 - cached_prefix_prob. We'll default cached_prefix_prob based on KV-cache hit rates per model (observed telemetry).
maria: Filed issue #3842 with repro steps and sample profile. Attaching a tiny script to reproduce locally.
aj: Thx. For the packer micro-opt, I can carve out a perf task for next sprint.
sophia: Can we also run a quick sweep: group_size in [32,64,96,128] with prepack=false and prepack=true to quantify tradeoffs? Add to the job matrix.
maria: Will add. Quick note: if anyone is debugging kernel chooser, add `--debug-kernel-score` to perf_driver to dump scoring table. Saved me a lot when chasing an unrelated fp8 fallback.
ryan: Nice. TL;DR: regression = pack overhead amplified by group_size 128 + prepack disabled. Immediate mitigation = prefer prepacked kernel via selector rule. Medium = packer optimizations + prepack-on-load option.
sophia: Agreed. :thumbsup:
aj: :+1:
maria: Thanks all. I'll post perf artifacts in the perf-run channel and update #3842 when I have the full sweep. :rocket:
